scope: Four complete collectible-card art studies; no game logic changes.

cards.name: Le serment du verger
cards.note: Enluminure nocturne, pomme rouge et titre gravé.
cards.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / collectible card design.
Create ONE finished original portrait-format collectible game card, full flat orthographic front, 2:3 aspect ratio, card fills image with no table/background/mockup perspective. Original fantasy trading-card craft and materiality, with a dominant illustration, a sculpted title plate at top and a small ivory rules panel below. Neo-retro hand-authored pixel painting: clear deliberate pixel clusters, early 16-bit adventure illustration, strong hand drawing, no photographic processing, no plastic 3D. Beautiful tangible card object rather than a computer dashboard. Black and BLUE dominant, ivory lettering/paper and restrained antique gold accents; NO overall brown cast. No animals or fantasy creatures, no franchise logos, no mana symbols, no rarity, cost, combat stats or flavor prose.
Text EXACTLY, concise and clearly readable:
Top title: "Cible"
Single rules sentence: "Accélère vers sa cible."
No other words, numbers or labels. A single recessed thin horizontal slider with a square brass thumb may sit at the bottom edge, with no numbers and no extra mechanism. Illustration fills about 60-65% of card. The rules text is large enough to read at small game-card size. Keep all text inside its plate and no cropping. No gradients in UI, no neon HUD.
DIRECTION 1 — LE SERMENT DU VERGER. A medieval illuminated manuscript meets an old fantasy trading card. Elaborate but economical blue enamel and old brass frame, an arched illustration window, tiny carved oak leaf corner details, tall elegant engraved ROMAN SERIF title like Perpetua Titling; rules in a warm readable Garamond-like book serif.
Picture: RED APPLE in the right foreground on a stone post, a single arrow precisely about to enter its center. A rugged human bowman in blue with a green cap is visible on the left middle ground aiming at it, with a distant blue castle and pale moon. The apple is the focal point, large and vivid, the line from bow to apple unmistakable. The apple is on the POST, never on a person's head. Angular medieval drawing, folktale atmosphere, deep lapis blue shadows and a few yellow highlights. Imaginative collectible illustration, no unnecessary people, no generic scenic landscape. Use the reference only for the human archery concept; redesign composition and frame completely.

cards.name: Le veilleur de l’Atlantique
cards.note: Scène de commandement, acier gravé et lumière rouge.
cards.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / original collectible card design.
ONE finished portrait-format collectible game card, full flat orthographic front, 2:3 ratio, fills image, no tabletop or perspective mockup. Physical collectible-card proportions and hierarchy: sculpted title plate at top, LARGE illustration about 60-65%, small IVORY rules panel beneath. Craft of a fantasy trading card adapted imaginatively to historical naval adventure. Neo-retro hand-authored pixel painting, bold readable pixel clusters and strong illustrated silhouettes. No photographic processing, plastic 3D, modern dashboard or futuristic HUD. Black/BLUE dominant, ivory and restrained metal accents. No animals, monsters, game logos, franchise branding, mana symbols, costs, rarity, combat stats, dates or flavor paragraphs.
Only text exactly:
Title: "Cible"
Rules: "Accélère vers sa cible."
No other lettering or numbers. Clear text comfortably within plates. At very bottom a single narrow recessed slider with a square brass thumb, no values.
Naval setting is fictional SECOND WORLD WAR ERA, 1940s, not modern submarines. Vintage periscopes, riveted steel, brass optics and wool uniforms. No political insignia, no real unit markings, no flags, no explosions or weapons firing. The concept AIM / TARGET must be visually unmistakable.
DIRECTION 3 — LE VEILLEUR DE L’ATLANTIQUE. Atmospheric illustrated collectible card with an ornamental blackened navy/STEEL frame, silver engraved corner flourishes resembling old nautical instruments, tiny brass screws, small compass rose motif. The shape and craftsmanship feel like a fantasy card, not an equipment UI.
Top title uses distinct COPPERPLATE engraved serif typography, wide chiselled small capitals. Rules use a clean old book serif.
Illustration: cramped 1940s submarine control room, a rugged middle-aged HUMAN naval officer at the LEFT in a blue wool sweater and unmarked officer cap, one eye pressed to a large brass-and-black vintage periscope. His hands grip the optical handles. At RIGHT an elegant circular optical-view inset is integrated INTO the painting, showing choppy cobalt Atlantic water, a distant unmarked freighter silhouette precisely centered under a bold ivory/yellow mechanical crosshair. The inset is large enough that AIM is recognizable instantly. Red lamp gives a small red accent on his cheek, deep blue shadows, amber brass highlights. Strong scene with human tension and vintage adventure, no tiny control-panel clutter. The reference gives the crosshair concept only; invent a richer scene and a full physical collectible card.
